newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Euromark vols ease, more rate cuts seen.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Euromark vols ease, more rate cuts seen.

text.p: Implied volatility levels for options on Euromarks on LIFFE drifted lower on Thursday amid a bullish market sentiment on further cuts in the German repo rate, traders said.
Earlier the Bundesbank council decided to keep the next two securities repurchase rate tenders at a fixed rate of three percent, the level at which the repo rate has been since August.

"Volatility is drifting down again in Euromarks," said a trader at a French brokerage in London. "People are still bullish for repo rate cuts, so with that in the market at the moment volatility is coming towards the bid side and easing."

Brokers quoted implied volatility levels on December options at 10.0 percent, compared with 11.36 percent at Wednesday's close. Further out March volatility was at 16.75 percent virtually unchanged from Wednesday.
A trader at a Swiss house in London said activity had been dominated by the Bundesbank council meeting, with some position taking ahead of the meeting.
He said a U.S. house had sold the March Euromark straddle at the 96.75 strike and bought 97.00 calls.
"That's a position which will benefit if interest rates are the same at maturity as they are now," the trader said.
March was the most actively traded month during Thursday's session, with around 5,000 lots of 96.75 and 97.00 call strikes, and 1,000 lots of 96.75 put strikes traded so far.
The underlying March Euromarks were trading at 96.79, up one basis point on the day at 1430 GMT.
